parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.part_stem: A loudspeaker oscillates with frequency $f$ to produce sound waves of wavelength $\lambda$. The loudspeaker makes $N$ oscillations in time $t$.
parts.text:
State expressions, in terms of some or all of the symbols $f$, $\lambda$ and $N$, for:

1. the distance moved by a wavefront in time $t$

2. time $t$.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Use your answers in (i) to deduce the equation relating the speed $v$ of the sound wave to $f$ and $\lambda$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The waveform of a sound wave is displayed on the screen of a cathode-ray oscilloscope (c.r.o.), as shown in Fig. 5.1.

{{figure:figure_5_1}}

Fig. 5.1

The time-base setting is $0.20\text{ ms cm}^{-1}$.

Determine the frequency of the sound wave.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.part_stem:
Two sources $S_1$ and $S_2$ of sound waves are positioned as shown in Fig. 5.2.

{{figure:figure_5_2}}

Fig. 5.2 (not to scale)

The sources emit coherent sound waves of wavelength $0.85\text{ m}$. A sound detector is moved parallel to the line $S_1S_2$ from a point X to a point Y. Alternate positions of maximum loudness L and minimum loudness Q are detected, as illustrated in Fig. 5.2.

Distance $S_1X$ is equal to distance $S_2X$. Distance $S_2Y$ is $7.40\text{ m}$.
parts.text: Explain what is meant by coherent waves.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State the phase difference between the two waves arriving at the position of minimum loudness Q that is closest to point X.
